description: A serious fungal disease of cereal crops that infects the heads of plants such as wheat and barley. It reduces grain yield and quality and can produce a toxic compound (mycotoxin) in the grain.
symptoms: One or more spikelets turn white while the rest remain green
Pink or orange fungal spores at the base of glumes
Whitish or pink fluffy fungal growth on infected heads in wet weather
Shriveled, lightweight and bleached kernels (tombstone kernels)
favorable_conditions: High humidity or continuous moisture for 36 hours
Presence of infected crop residues in the field
spread: Rain splash spreading spores between plants
Movement of contaminated crop residues or grain
management: Use resistant or tolerant cereal varieties
Rotate crops and avoid planting cereals after corn
Scout fields during flowering for symptoms
Harvest early when infection risk is high
Dry and aerate grain properly during storage
biological_control: Trichoderma species used as biological antagonists in soil or seed treatment
Beneficial microbes to suppress Fusarium in crop residues
chemical_control: Apply triazole fungicides (e.g. tebuconazole, prothioconazole, metconazole) during flowering stage
Use registered fungicides according to local agricultural recommendations
prevention: Rotate crops for at least 2 years with non-host crops
Manage crop residues by tillage or decomposition
Use proper irrigation management during flowering
Separate and test contaminated grain before feeding livestock
impact: Contaminated grain affects food processing, malting and biofuel production
High DON levels reduce feed intake and immunity in livestock
source: Plant pathology literature on cereal diseases
